techniques.name: Capoed Acoustic Fingerpicking
techniques.description: Plucking bass notes with pick or thumb while fingers simultaneously fret melodic hammer-on and pull-off fills

notes: Capo placed securely on the 7th fret transforms open D shapes into concert A Major
High string tension at the 7th fret produces a bright, bell-like harpsichord timbre
Keep wrist relaxed to alternate smoothly between bass strums and treble flourishes
sequence: Thumb picks root on open D string (4th string)
Fingers pluck B and high E strings
Pinky executes hammer-on on 3rd fret high E, pulling off back to 2nd fret
tips: Use a high-quality capo with adjustable tension to prevent intonation sharpness
Practice the syncopated accents on the upbeat 'and' of beat 2

techniques.name: Odd-Meter Time Signature Shifts
techniques.description: Navigating George Harrison's intricate bridge meter cycle through 11/8, 4/4, and 7/8 measures

notes: Influenced by George Harrison's study of Indian classical rhythmic cycles (tala)
Subdivides measures into groupings of 3s and 2s (e.g., 3+3+3+2 for 11/8)
Moog synthesizer and acoustic guitar lock together on the synchronized stabs
sequence: Count 1-2-3, 1-2-3, 1-2-3, 1-2 over F to C chord transition
Resolve into standard 4/4 measure on G to D resolution
Sustain final A7 turnaround to reset the pulse
tips: Tap your foot on the primary pulses rather than counting individual eighth notes
Lock in with Ringo Starr's accented handclaps and snare rimshots

sections.name: Intro Riff
sections.description: The world-famous acoustic guitar opening featuring ringing D-shape arpeggios and high E string melodic fills.
notes: Fret standard open D chord shape with capo on fret 7
Execute the high E hammer-on/pull-off with the pinky cleanly
Let the open strings ring into one another for lush acoustic resonance

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Gentle acoustic backing underneath George Harrison's warm lead vocals with moving bass notes.
notes: Smooth dynamics supporting the vocal storytelling
Accentuate the bass note walkup from E to G# on the E7 chord
Keep the 16th-note strumming wrist loose and flexible

sections.name: Bridge (Sun, Sun, Sun)
sections.description: The escalating rhythmic cycle repeating 'Sun, sun, sun, here it comes' with ascending Moog synthesizer fills.
notes: Internalize the 11/8 meter as 3+3+3+2 eighth notes
Maintain strict pick attack on the downstrokes for percussive impact
Build dynamic volume on each repetition leading into the triumphant chorus

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Return to the signature intro motif, gradually slowing tempo into a peaceful, chime-like final D major strum.
notes: Delicate pick attack to let the harmonics chime clearly
Allow the final open D chord to ring out until complete silence

beginner.title: Capo Placement & Basic Chord Shapes
steps: Clamp capo on the 7th fret and verify all six strings are in tune
Practice switching between open D, G, and A7 chord shapes relative to the capo
Play the basic verse progression at 90 BPM with steady eighth-note downstrokes

intermediate.title: Master the Intro Riff & Melodic Embellishments
steps: Isolate the pinky hammer-on and pull-off on the 1st string while holding the D chord
Practice the string-skipping arpeggios that connect D to G
Bring the intro up to full album tempo of 129 BPM with swing feel

advanced.title: Odd-Meter Bridge Synchronization
steps: Subdivide the 11/8 and 7/8 measures in the bridge into rhythmic sub-pulses
Coordinate the syncopated chord stabs with the vocal phrasing
Perform the entire song seamlessly from memory with vocal accompaniment

commonMistakes: Placing the capo too close to the fret wire causing string buzzing or sharp intonation
Muting the open high E string with the fretting hand while attempting the D chord hammer-ons
Losing count during the bridge's 11/8 meter changes
practiceRoutine: 5 min: Tune guitar thoroughly with capo clamped on 7th fret
10 min: Slow repetition of the intro pinky hammer-on sequence at 80 BPM
15 min: Metronome drills on the bridge time signature transitions
10 min: Full run-through focusing on fluid acoustic dynamics and timing
focusAreas: Independent pinky finger control for melodic hammer-ons
Polyrhythmic counting across the bridge meter shifts
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 80 BPM and practice the intro arpeggio in 4/4
Set metronome to eighth notes (258 BPM) to count the 11/8 bridge measures accurately
Gradually accelerate to full performance speed of 129 BPM
